links.outcome: Deployed LLM performance on multi-turn stroke history-taking, urgency, and safety versus exam-style benchmarks
links.effect: Eighteen models evaluated; top model scored 87.4% with zero critical mistakes, only two met safety threshold (≥80%, zero critical mistakes); eleven models made 17 critical mistakes despite strong exam-level knowledge.
links.quote: Two leaders met the safety threshold.

links.outcome: Critical mistakes in emergency stroke management by LLMs in multi-turn conversations
links.effect: Eleven models made 17 critical mistakes, including failure to confirm labs or blood glucose before t-PA, surgery before airway stabilization, omission of cervical vascular evaluation, and t-PA outside indication.
links.quote: Eleven models made 17 critical mistakes, including failure to confirm laboratory results or blood glucose before t-PA, surgery before airway stabilization, omission of cervical vascular evaluation, and t-PA outside its indication.

unlisted_practices: Multi-turn conversational benchmark with capped history-taking questions, scored by specialist physicians rather than LLM-as-judge

screen.reason: Empirical study developing and applying a multi-turn conversational benchmark (with simulated patients) to evaluate LLM clinical history taking, urgency assessment, and safety in stroke care.
